title: Slicing a smooth morphism
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a
smooth morphism of schemes. Then
there exists an etale covering $\{U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ such that
$U_i\to S$ factors as $U_i\to V_i\to S$ where $V_i\to S$ is etale and
$U_i\to V_i$ is a smooth morphism of affine schemes, which has a
section, and has geometrically
connected fibres.
(*Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, [Tag `0EY4`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EY4) = Lemma
37.38.8.*)

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $x\in X$. Choose affine opens $S_0\subseteq S$ about $f(x)$ and $X_0\subseteq f^{-1}(S_0)$ about $x$. Let $f_0:X_0\to S_0$ be the restriction. The affine-basis statement gives these opens, the smooth-restriction statement gives smoothness of $f_0$, and the affine-schemes and affine-permanence statements give that $f_0$ is affine, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. It suffices to construct the required factorization over $X_0,S_0$ with $x$ in its image; composing with the open inclusions will return it to $X,S$.

source.place: Tag 0EY4, lemma-cover-smooth-by-special; pointwise version of the argument in Slicing.lean:225-349

proof.text: Apply the fibre-component-neighbourhood statement to $f_0,x$, which is permitted since smoothness includes local finite presentation, hence local finite type: an affine presentation $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by the images of $t_1,\ldots,t_n$. Obtain $W$ containing $x$ with $W\cap f_0^{-1}(f_0(x))$ inside its component. The scheme-theoretic fibre is smooth over its residue field by clause (2) of the smooth-base-change statement and has this same subspace topology. Density of finite separable closed points applied to its nonempty open $W\cap f_0^{-1}(f_0(x))$ gives $x^{\prime}$ there, with finite separable residue field over $\kappa(f_0(x))$. Thus $x,x^{\prime}$ lie in the same fibre component.

source.place: Tag 0EY4, lemma-cover-smooth-by-special; pointwise version of the argument in Slicing.lean:225-349

proof.text: Apply the separable-point etale-slice statement to $f_0,x^{\prime}$. It gives affine $Z$, $i:Z\to X_0$, and $z\in Z$ with $i(z)=x^{\prime}$ and $r=i$ followed by $f_0$ etale. Put $P=X_0\times_{S_0}Z$, with projections $p$ and $g$. The fibre-product universal property gives a section $\sigma=(i,\mathrm{id}_Z)$ of $g$. Clause (2) of smooth base change makes $g$ smooth, and affine permanence makes it affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The projection $p$ is etale, being the base change of $r$.

source.place: Tag 0EY4, lemma-cover-smooth-by-special; pointwise version of the argument in Slicing.lean:225-349

proof.text: Apply the component-image statement with $a=\sigma(z)$: its first projection is $x^{\prime}$. Since $x$ lies in that same component, there is $a_0\in P$ over $x$ lying in the fibre component of $\sigma(z)$ over $z$. Apply the relative-section-component statement to $g,\sigma$ to obtain an open $P_0\subseteq P$ containing the section and the entire component in question, with geometrically irreducible fibres over $Z$. In particular $a_0\in P_0$. Its restriction $h:P_0\to Z$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 0EY4, lemma-cover-smooth-by-special; pointwise version of the argument in Slicing.lean:225-349

proof.text: Choose an affine open $A\subseteq P_0$ containing $a_0$. Put $T=h(A)\subseteq Z$. Smoothness gives flatness and local finite presentation; the flat-lfp open-map statement therefore makes $T$ open. Let $k:A\to T$ be the restricted map. It is smooth by smooth restriction. Set $t=k(a_0)$. By smooth base change its fibre over $t$ is smooth over $\kappa(t)$, and by density it contains a finite separable closed point $a^{\prime}$. Apply the etale-slice statement again, now to $k,a^{\prime}$, to obtain affine $Z^{\prime}$, $j:Z^{\prime}\to A$, and $z^{\prime}\in Z^{\prime}$ with $j(z^{\prime})=a^{\prime}$ and $r^{\prime}=k\circ j:Z^{\prime}\to T$ etale.

source.place: Tag 0EY4, lemma-cover-smooth-by-special; pointwise version of the argument in Slicing.lean:225-349

proof.text: Set $U=A\times_T Z^{\prime}$, $V=Z^{\prime}$, and $q:U\to Z^{\prime}$ the second projection. It is smooth by smooth base change and has section $(j,\mathrm{id}_{Z^{\prime}})$ by the fibre-product universal property. Its map to $X_0$ is the first projection followed by $A\hookrightarrow P_0\hookrightarrow P$ and $p$. Each open inclusion is etale, the first projection is the base change of $r^{\prime}$, and $p$ is etale, so this composite is etale. The map $V=Z^{\prime}\to T$ is $r^{\prime}$ and is etale; the inclusion $T\hookrightarrow Z$ is etale as an open immersion, and $Z\to S_0$ is $r$ and is etale. Applying etale composition twice proves that $V\to S_0$ is etale. The two composites to $S_0$ agree by the defining equality of each fibre product.

source.place: Tag 0EY4, lemma-cover-smooth-by-special; pointwise version of the argument in Slicing.lean:225-349

proof.text: The map $A\to Z$ is between affine schemes, hence affine. Its base change to the affine scheme $Z^{\prime}$ is affine and has affine source by affine permanence. Since both $A\to Z$ and $Z^{\prime}\to Z$ factor through the open $T$, the universal property identifies $A\times_ZZ^{\prime}$ with $A\times_TZ^{\prime}=U$: any pair of maps agreeing in $Z$ agrees in $T$ because an open inclusion is a monomorphism. Therefore $U$ is affine, and $V=Z^{\prime}$ is affine by construction.

source.place: Tag 0EY4, lemma-cover-smooth-by-special; pointwise version of the argument in Slicing.lean:225-349

proof.text: For any point of $V$ and any extension field of its residue field, the corresponding fibre of $U\to V$ is, by base change of the open immersion $A\hookrightarrow P_0$ and the fibre-product universal property, an open subscheme of the corresponding field base change of a fibre of $P_0\to Z$. The latter is irreducible by the relative-component statement and the definition of geometric irreducibility. The former is nonempty because the section of $q$ base changes to a rational point. A nonempty open subset of an irreducible space is irreducible: two nonempty relatively open subsets are nonempty opens of the ambient irreducible space and so intersect. It is therefore connected, since a disconnection would give two disjoint nonempty opens. This proves geometrically connected fibres for $q$. The same argument without the field extension shows $A_t$ irreducible, since it is an open of the irreducible fibre $(P_0)_t$ and contains $a_0$.

source.place: Tag 0EY4, lemma-cover-smooth-by-special; pointwise version of the argument in Slicing.lean:225-349

proof.text: The points $a_0,a^{\prime}$ are in the same connected component of the fibre of $k$ over $t$, since this fibre is irreducible and nonempty as just shown. Apply the component-image statement to $k$, the etale morphism $r^{\prime}$, and the section point $(j(z^{\prime}),z^{\prime})$ of $U$. It gives a point $u\in U$ projecting to $a_0$, hence mapping to the original $x$ in $X_0$. This supplies pointwise coverage, without claiming that an open dense union must be the whole fibre.

source.place: Tag 0EY4, lemma-cover-smooth-by-special; pointwise version of the argument in Slicing.lean:225-349

proof.text: Compose the maps to $X_0,S_0$ with their inclusions into $X,S$. Open inclusions and composites of etale maps are etale, while $q$, its section, affine source and target, and its geometric fibres have not changed. The factorization equality follows by associativity and the equality $X_0\to S_0\to S=X_0\to X\to S$. Choose one such diagram for each $x\in X$ and index by the set of points of $X$. For each $x$, the point $u$ just constructed maps to $x$, so the family is jointly surjective and therefore an etale covering. If $X$ is empty, use the empty family.
